conviction_note: Q4/FY26 trading update for a year whose guide (AOP £234-242m) already brackets a tight consensus (£238.0m, 8 forecasts, min 235.6 / max 240.5); the company's own 'Q4 started positively, strong volume momentum' plus Greggs' improving Q3 and a serial-upgrader record lean the print to the upper half of the range (+1% on the bar), but the stock has already run +6% in five sessions into the date and the interims showed this name can fall 9% on cash, so p_up sits at 55 on a 4.5% scale; the findings sum (+0.9) and the scaled number (+0.45) agree in sign and differ only because the run-up and cash risk act on p_up, not on the findings.

session_check: bmo — the issuer's 28 Aug 2026 RNS fixes the date (13 Oct 2026) but not the hour; every prior Greencore trading statement this year went out at 07:00 London (Q1 TU 29 Jan 07:00, interims 27 May 07:00, Q3 TU 22 Jul 07:00, per https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/GNC), so pre-open by the issuer's own pattern, not a timestamp for this release
positioning_check: FCA aggregated net short 2.89% of shares (position date 2026-10-05, register read 2026-10-09) against 2.79% previously: +0.10pt, slightly building, not crowded (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv). findings.finding: Greencore's own Q3 statement said Q4 'started positively, with strong volume momentum continuing from the latter half of Q3' plus a first combined new-business win launching in August, and this management has raised or beaten at successive trading updates (Q4 FY24 +8.8%, Q3 FY26 +8.5% on the day), which points FY26 AOP to the upper half of the £234-242m range against a £238.0m consensus sitting at the midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 upgrade above consensus: +8.48% (22 Jul 2026); Q4 FY24 upgrade: +8.77% (8 Oct 2024); Q4 FY25 update: low single digit; FY26 'in line' at interims with weak cash: -9.02% (27 May 2026). Upgrades outside the range have paid; landing inside a guided range has not been tested.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus already sits at the guide midpoint and the stock is +6% in five sessions. What is not in the bar is the upper-half outcome: if the market had priced it, the Vuma consensus would sit near £240-242m rather than £238.0m, and its max (£240.5m) is still under the top of the guide. It lands inside company guidance, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Greggs Q3 (separate company, separate document) shows UK food-to-go improving through Jul-Sep: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/greggs--grg/q3-trading-update/9797639

findings.finding: Greggs' Q3 RNS (13 weeks to 26 Sep 2026, the same weeks as Greencore's Q4) reported company-managed LFL +3.4% against +2.6% year to date, 'trading improved across the quarter... more settled weather in August and September', and a 'modestly improved outcome for 2026', a direct read on UK food-to-go demand, Greencore's largest category (sandwiches, 'Food for now' 50% of Q3 revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume ahead of market was the lead line in the +8.48% Q3 reaction (22 Jul 2026); legacy Bakkavor volume decline was part of the -9.02% interim reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: GNC rose +3.3% on 30 Sep 2026 (246.0 to 254.0p, Yahoo bars) and then gave it back by 2 Oct (244.4p), before the 5-session run to 258.6p. Greggs is a retailer, not a Greencore customer, so transmission is a hypothesis; sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: Worldpanel take-home grocery +3.3% in the four weeks to 12 Jul 2026 with convenience trips +7m: https://www.checkout.ie/retail/uk-grocery-prices-ease-as-world-cup-and-sunshine-boost-sales-worldpanel-227422

findings.finding: Worldpanel shows the UK grocery market strong in July (take-home sales +3.3%, 4 weeks to 12 Jul, inflation 2.6%, convenience trips up 7m) but slowing into Greencore's Q4 tail (sales +2.0% in the 4 weeks to 6 Sep against inflation of 2.3%, i.e. roughly flat to negative volume), so the market backdrop for Q4 volume is mixed rather than a tailwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Greencore benchmarks its volume against the grocery market each update (Q3: +0.7% vs market -0.4%); outperformance was rewarded on 22 Jul 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Public monthly series that every covering analyst reads; it is in the price and is filed because it is the broad series the Greggs proxy must not contradict. The September read is from search snippets of the 2026-09-15 Worldpanel release (https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/uk-grocery-inflation-edges-higher-over-last-month-worldpanel/), snippet_only.

findings.finding: The Q4/FY26 trading update was moved from 8 October (stated in the 22 July RNS) to 13 October by a dedicated 28 August notice that gives no reason; unexplained.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price: a five-day shift announced six weeks ahead with no stated cause, which could be diary or could be to pair the statement with a US-disposal update. An unexplained fact is worth 0; filed so it is not lost.

findings.finding: Cash is the line that has moved this name the wrong way: H1 free cash flow was -£76.0m and net debt £817.6m (2.3x) and the stock fell 9.02% on the interims despite an 'in line' outlook; the Q3 RNS says the working-capital outflow 'has already started to reverse' and guides a neutral net working capital position by FY26 end, against a consensus FY26 net debt of £744.4m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interims 27 May 2026: negative FCF and an in-line guide, -9.02%; Q3 22 Jul 2026: 'positive cashflow generation' alongside the upgrade, +8.48% (RBC said the update should calm working-capital concerns).
findings.why_not_priced: Not knowable in advance: the outcome sits inside the company's own guide (neutral WC) and nothing published since 22 July says which way it will land, so sized at 0 with a deliberately wide, left-skewed range. If a Q4 trading statement reports net debt at all, this is the line where a miss would show.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly the same way as the priced lean (+1.37, mostly the 2.89% short) but against the +6.07% five-session run-up, which already discounts a solid statement; that run-up plus the cash line is why p_up is 55 rather than the 57-60 the findings alone would carry.

lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' / inside-guidance rule: the upper-half-of-range finding lands inside the company's own £234-242m guide, cut from +0.6 to +0.4
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): added the working-capital/net-debt line as its own finding at 0.0 with a left-skewed range, and moved p_up from 57 to 55
'Size the move on what is new, let reaction history move p_up': abs_move_pct held at 4.5 despite the tight, pre-bracketed guide; not shrunk for uncertainty
